text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government tells parliament 50,000 Kuwaitis are expected to seek jobs over the next five years. MPs discussed on Tuesday unemployment and measures by the state to secure jobs. Over 90 percent of the Kuwaiti workforce is hired by the state.

- Kuwait to offer 60 million Gulf Bank shares for public subscription in February. An auction earlier in January for 30 million Gulf Bank shares earned the state $57 million. Since 1994 the state has been privatising its holdings in several local firms and banks.
- Government to reduce foreign civil servants by 10 percent annually.

- European-African plan to divide Sudan into a Christian south and an Arab Moslem north, eastern European diplomatic sources say. The British-designed plan was set after consultation with the United States. The Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), a mainly southern group which has been fighting the army in southern Sudan since 1983, is now working together with the northern opponents to Sudan's Islamist government.
- Kuwait releases 90 prisoners at deportation centre over the past two months, official says. Kuwait has announced plans to close the centre often criticised by parliamentarians.
